story: At 8:17 on this partly cloudy Wednesday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at home carefully test-fitting light strips and speaker mounts on his golf cart, jotting measurements for the review form. Across the way, Donna is restocking her pickleball bag and packing a spare paddle for Gary's game next Tuesday, all in good spirits. Hal has set off down Magnolia Loop on his dutiful rounds, while Rosa, determined as ever, is chopping aromatics and making a sofrito base in her kitchen to portion out for Friday.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Test-fit the light strips and speaker mounts on the cart, measuring and noting each for the review form
Donna (donna pickleball bag): Restock the bag and pack Gary's spare paddle for next Tuesday
Hal headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Start prepping what keeps: chop aromatics, make the sofrito base, and portion it for Friday

gary.thought_process: I'm home at the workbench at 8:17 AM, no one around. Last tick I bench-tested the light strings and speaker wiring and sketched what shows from the street. Now I should finish the job: get the cart rigging ready and the details lined up for the Architectural Review form (L-01), since exterior mods visible from the street need approval before the parade. Holiday lighting is allowed starting Thanksgiving (L-04), so I shouldn't hang anything on the street side yet. Best move is to work on the golf cart itself, mounting things in a way I can describe accurately on the form, and keep the speaker volume in mind for quiet hours (L-03).

parameters.content: Test-fit the light strips and speaker mounts on the cart, measuring and noting each for the review form

donna.thought_process: It's Wednesday morning and I'm home alone with no one in sight. Yesterday's session with Gary went beautifully, and I already penciled in next week's slot on the club calendar. The pickleball bag is right here, so I should make sure Gary's spare paddle is packed and the bag is ready. That keeps my ladder plan moving without bothering anyone this early.

parameters.content: Restock the bag and pack Gary's spare paddle for next Tuesday

hal.thought_process: I've scanned the loop twice already and logged the tally. Nobody's in sight, it's a pleasant morning, and I've been sitting on this paperwork long enough. The only place to actually file the flamingo and cart reports is the architectural review committee, and that means heading out. Rosa's coffee is Thursday, so today is for getting my business in order. Gary's paperwork gets checked line by line, Donna gets a fair count.

parameters.content: Heading out to walk the loop, get an honest flamingo count in person, and see what's parked on the grass before I file anything.

rosa.thought_process: It's Wednesday morning and I'm alone at home. Friday's dinner is the big goal: all three neighbors at one table. I've already counted chairs, laid out the good plates and tested the place cards, so the table is essentially ready. The shopping list is finalized and the shift schedule is confirmed clear for Friday evening and Thursday 8 AM for Hal. The next useful thing is to prep ahead in the kitchen so Friday isn't a scramble. I'll sort out what can be made today, since I'll be out buying groceries soon anyway. No need to repeat the schedule check.

parameters.content: Start prepping what keeps: chop aromatics, make the sofrito base, and portion it for Friday

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
